root_shock.label: Grid modernization and resilience investment
root_shock.mechanism: Utilities increased transmission, substation, distribution, and resilience investment to replace aging infrastructure, harden the grid against extreme weather, integrate new generation, and relieve congestion; this equipment demand exists independently of AI data-center load growth.
causal_chain: aging assets, extreme-weather exposure, and generation interconnection needs raise utility grid capital plans
funded transmission and substation projects convert those plans into orders for structures and high-voltage equipment
persistent utility capital spending raises demand for constrained transformer manufacturing capacity

evidence.summary: Valmont's June 2026 utility strategy materials identified utility capital-expenditure tailwinds, incremental utility sales, a visible project pipeline, and brownfield expansion as linked operating drivers.

EIA reported 2023 utility transmission investment of $27.7 billion and distribution investment of $50.9 billion, with spending driven by aging-equipment replacement, resilience, renewable integration, and substation and transformer upgrades.
DOE announced $1.5 billion for four transmission projects intended to improve reliability and resilience, relieve congestion, and expand access to electricity supply.
